title: Microsoft Teams: organisers choose who controls production tools in meetings with presenters and webinars
summary: Hold: the licensing gap is stated too broadly. Microsoft publishes licensing for the event production capabilities this option controls, including Manage what attendees see; only separate licensing for the new dropdown remains unspecified. The meeting option, default availability and town hall configuration path are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing Who has control of production tools for meetings with presenters and webinars.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams is introducing a new meeting option for meetings with presenters and webinars that allows organizers to specify who has control of production tools during an event.
claims.fix: Add: 'Microsoft Learn currently differs from the notice: its feature comparison marks this option unavailable for meetings and events up to 1,000 attendees, and available for events optimized for large audiences.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/meetings-events-feature-comparison.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Plan for Teams events lists no admin control over the town hall production-tools selection.
claims.quote: Who has control of production tools | No control. | Organizers can choose specific organizers, co-organizers, or presenters who can control production tools

claims.claim: No tenant UI switch or automation for this production-tools option is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Who has control of production tools policy default; production tools Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. Opened plan-events, Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no feature-specific tenant switch or parameter found.

claims.claim: The town hall organiser path is Calendar > town hall > View event > Manage event > Meeting options > Production tools > Who has control of production tools.
claims.quote: Select Calendar in Teams. Select a town hall. Select View event > Manage event. Select Meeting options. In Production tools, select an option from the Who has control of production tools dropdown menu:

claims.claim: No API or automation for the organiser's production-tools selection is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: production tools onlineMeeting Graph; production tools Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. Opened Graph beta onlineMeeting and virtualEventSettings, Teams meeting/events policy references and Support production-tools article; no matching selection property or command found.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy syntax lists no production-tools parameter.
claims.quote: Searched: production-tools parameters in https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy. Read the complete syntax list: no production-tools parameter is listed; the module is MicrosoftTeams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap, supplied notice and cited Support article name no licence, price or meter for this new option.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams production tools license webinars. Read the complete roadmap record, MC1443520 and Support production-tools article; none names a licence, price or meter for the new dropdown. This limited absence does not establish that platform licensing is unpublished.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is not yet published, and Microsoft Learn documents no licensing for the option's capabilities.
claims.quote: Advanced event features: These licenses provide the full Teams events feature set. They include the foundational capabilities plus advanced features such as event workflows, customization, production controls, monitoring, insights, and higher engagement event capacity.
claims.fix: Retain licensing.model 'unknown' only for separate licensing of the new dropdown. Replace the unqualified unpublished-licensing statements in licensing.notes, Cost and licensing, Open questions and the cost rationale with: 'Microsoft publishes licensing for the event capabilities this option controls: Manage what attendees see is an advanced event feature, available with licences including Office 365 E1, E3 and E5 and Microsoft 365 E3, E5 and E7. Separate licensing or a meter for the new production-control dropdown is not specified.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/events-licensing. Retain the low cost rating for the documented communication and training work.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes assigning production responsibilities as reducing unintended changes during live events.
claims.quote: This helps organizers assign production responsibilities to designated individuals, improving event management and reducing the risk of unintended changes during live events.
